title: Global Oil Markets — Executive Daily Brief (2026-08-19)
executive_summary: Most material drivers today: (1) EIA shows a sizeable U.S. crude build but another distillate draw into peak demand, tightening diesel cracks even as refineries run near 97%; (2) Panama Canal will impose deeper Neopanamax draft cuts starting August 26, heightening ton‑mile and freight risk for USGC–Asia refined products, LPG/LNG; (3) Strait of Hormuz/Red Sea risk remains elevated with recent incidents and only partial, fragile improvements, sustaining prompt risk premia and re‑routing; (4) Tight middle distillate balances in ARA and lean LSFO at Fujairah keep regional bunkers and gasoil pricing firm despite higher residual stocks.

developments.headline: U.S. EIA weekly: Crude builds 4.4 mb; gasoline +0.7 mb; distillate −1.5 mb; utilization 97.2% (week ending Aug 14)
developments.summary: EIA’s weekly report released today shows crude inventories at 428.8 mb (≈at the 5‑yr avg), gasoline inventories 5% below the 5‑yr avg after a 0.7 mb build, and distillates 13% below the 5‑yr avg after a 1.5 mb draw. Total commercial petroleum inventories rose 8.8 mb. Refinery runs increased to 17.4 mb/d with 97.2% utilization; gasoline output rose to 9.7 mb/d, while distillate production slipped to 5.2 mb/d.
developments.why_it_matters: - Diesel/gasoil remains the tight leg in the barrel into late summer, supportive for ULSD/ICE gasoil cracks and USGC/ARA diesel diffs even as crude builds. - High utilization limits upside to cracks if product demand wobbles, but the distillate deficit vs. 5‑yr average argues for continued strength in middle‑distillate spreads and prompt backwardation. - The crude build amid lower imports (−746 kb/d w/w) suggests domestic balances loosened via runs and products, not import surges; watch for export response from USGC this week.

developments.headline: Panama Canal to tighten Neopanamax draft: 48 ft on Aug 26; 47.5 ft on Sept 3
developments.summary: The Panama Canal Authority confirmed further draft reductions for Neopanamax locks to 48 ft (14.63 m) effective Aug 26 and 47.5 ft (14.48 m) on Sept 3, citing low lake levels and ongoing water management. ACP says transits/day unchanged, but deeper‑draft cargoes will face payload trims.
developments.why_it_matters: - USGC → Asia refined products and LPG/LNG flows face higher lift-costs (lightening, partial loads) and/or re‑routing via Suez/Cape, lifting ton‑mile demand and product tanker and LPG/LNG freight into Sep. - Marginal barrels to Asia from USGC (gasoline, diesel, VGO/VLSFO blendstocks, LPG) could price up vs. local alternatives; Asia spot diffs may firm for grades/routes most exposed to Canal constraints.

developments.headline: Strait of Hormuz/Red Sea: elevated maritime risk persists; only partial normalization since June
developments.summary: S&P Global reports through June–July that attacks and military activity periodically disrupted transits through Hormuz, with some vessels taking risk‑mitigating routings and AIS dark activity. A June MoU framework aimed at easing flows has not fully normalized risk, and incidents continued into late June/early July; market commentators and price action this week remain sensitive to headlines.
developments.why_it_matters: - Sustained geopolitical risk premium supports prompt Brent/ICE gasoil backwardation and raises marine insurance and freight costs for AG/Red Sea trade lanes. - Fujairah has acted as a buffer hub; inventory and bunker premia dynamics there transmit to ARA/Asia product diffs. Maintain contingency for reroutes via Cape of Good Hope and for sporadic loadings/deliveries slippage.

developments.headline: ARA and Fujairah product balances diverge: ARA middle distillates tight; Fujairah residuals swell, LSFO lean
developments.summary: Insights Global/ENGINE indicate ARA gasoil inventories fell in early August vs July with strong barge demand and logistics bottlenecks; LSMGO prices surged ~24% m/m into early Aug. At Fujairah, FOIZ/S&P Global data show residual fuel oil inventories averaged 61% higher in July vs June amid greater regional supply, while LSFO supply remained comparatively tighter, keeping LSFO bunker premia firm at times.
developments.why_it_matters: - ARA diesel tightness and barge scarcity elevate inland premiums and support ICE gasoil cracks; Rotterdam LSMGO strength can spill into Northwest Europe jet and diesel markets. - Fujairah’s heavier residual build pressures HSFO/VLSFO spreads regionally; tight LSFO keeps delivered VLSFO relatively supported—relevant for ships diverting around chokepoints and for East‑of‑Suez bunker cost baselines.

portfolio_implications: Favor long diesel cracks (ICE gasoil/ULSD) vs. gasoline near term; distillate stocks remain 13% below 5‑yr avg despite high U.S. runs.
Maintain overweight on product and LPG carrier exposure into September as Panama draft cuts tighten payloads and extend ton‑miles.
Keep hedges for Gulf/Red Sea/Hormuz disruption: long prompt Brent timespreads or downside puts on freight‑sensitive routes to manage volatility.
For bunker buyers, consider HSFO/VLSFO optimization: Fujairah residual builds argue for tactical HSFO procurement where scrubber‑equipped; LSFO premia risk persists where supply is lean.
risks: A rapid de‑escalation around Hormuz would compress risk premia and timespreads, weakening prompt cracks and freight—hedge unwind risk.
Deeper‑than‑planned Panama restrictions or a shift to transit caps would further tighten global product and LPG/LNG freight, amplifying delivered prices in Asia/LatAm.
U.S. demand softness (gasoline and especially jet) could flip cracks lower if refinery runs stay near 97% and exports underperform.
Unexpected U.S. Gulf Coast weather disruptions could tighten products quickly and reverse today’s crude build.
opportunities: Exploit arbitrage windows USGC→LatAm/Europe for diesel and jet while ARA barge constraints persist.
Lock in time‑charters or optionality on LR/MR tonnage exposed to Canal/Cape diversions ahead of September.
Bunker procurement: secure HSFO where builds are evident; negotiate LSFO term premiums at Fujairah and Singapore before Q4 demand uptick.
watch_items: Next two EIA weeklies (Aug 21–28 loadings) for confirmation that distillate draws persist despite high runs.
ACP updates: any move from draft to daily‑transit limits would be materially more bullish freight and product diffs.
FEDCom/FOIZ weekly stock prints for signs that LSFO tightness eases or HSFO builds extend into August.
ARA weekly stocks and barge market conditions for middle‑distillate relief or further tightening into September turnarounds.
